answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled audit confirms fraud. Creating a thousand identities does not multiply influence for free: each must tie up capital, and each risky submission exposes that capital to loss. The stake should scale with the value at risk, while audits make colluding accounts share a spiral of expected penalties. An orchard or timber label may name a task, but neither grants extra voting weight.
